answer: One concrete defense binds each agent to a non-parallelizable verifiable delay function. Every identity must keep extending a sequential VDF chain signed by its cipher key, composed step by step like an unbroken sonnet line that no extra cores can shortcut. A single ferrous server sustains exactly one live chain in real time, so running N identities demands N physical machines humming continuously. The attacker cost is therefore linear: N times the hardware plus N times the electricity, with no pooling or batching to dilute it.
